## Results

- Analytic pipeline built on 27 NHANES 2017-2020 files (15,560 participants in the raw merge)
- Top-10 variable rankings per method (e.g., SIR1 led by serum globulin/total protein/albumin; LASSO and SHAP led by age, arthritis history, COPD history, income)
- Presented as a JSM 2025 poster

## The problem

Which routinely collected clinical and laboratory measures carry signal about depression severity, and do different variable-ranking methods agree?

## What I built

NHANES 2017-Mar 2020 pre-pandemic files merged on SEQN; PHQ-9 items modeled with brms cumulative-logit IRT (equal discrimination) to get latent severity; predictors cleaned (NZV, correlation filter, scaling); SIR with GMM-derived slices, PCA, cross-validated LASSO, and XGBoost+SHAP each rank variables; GAMs refit on top-10 variables per method.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Could inform which low-cost measures are worth including in behavioral-health screening or readiness-risk models (e.g., Army H2F/medical readiness), but no decision framing is stated.
:::

## Tools

R, brms, cmdstanr, mclust, glmnet, xgboost, SHAPforxgboost, mgcv, caret, gt
